Why go: a private speedboat to Pig Island

A private speedboat turns the southern islands into a flexible half day for your group. For 11,950 THB per boat you get a speedboat with captain and crew for 5–6 hours, for up to 10 guests: about 1,490 THB each for a group of eight, and 1,195 THB each for ten. From Thong Krut pier the reef at Koh Tan is only 10–15 minutes away, so almost all of your time is spent in the water and on the beaches, not travelling.

The core route is Koh Tan for snorkelling over a shallow coral reef close to the beach, and Koh Madsum (Pig Island) for the pigs, the white sand and a swim. What you pay for is choice. You decide the order, how long to stay at each stop and when to leave. If time and sea allow, the captain can add Koh Rap, a quieter island with a long beach, or another bay along the coast. Start at 08:30 to reach the islands before most shared boats, or at 14:00 for quieter beaches and the late light.

Speedboat or longtail? The private longtail costs 5,950 THB for up to 8 guests and is slower, louder and wetter in chop. The speedboat is drier and quicker, takes two more guests and has the range to add extra islands. For two or three people the longtail is better value; for groups of 6–10, celebrations or anyone who wants to cover more water, the speedboat makes more sense.

Suggested routes

  • Classic half day (5–6 hours): Koh Tan reef, Koh Madsum beach and pigs, lunch at a beach restaurant on either island.
  • Three islands: add Koh Rap's long, quiet beach if the sea allows. Ask when you book. For a set three-island day on a longtail, see the three-islands private boat.
  • Afternoon and sunset: start at 14:00, snorkel while the sun is high, then finish on Koh Madsum as the light turns gold.
  • Full day around Koh Rap: see the Koh Rap full-day private boat.

Who this tour is for

  • Groups of 6–10 friends or family, where private costs little more per head than shared seats.
  • Birthdays, hen and stag groups, and families with young children who want their own space and pace.
  • Snorkellers who want longer at the reef, and photographers who want the beach before the crowds.
  • Anyone who wants more than two islands in a half day.

Who should choose another tour

  • Two to four people on a budget: the private longtail or the shared speedboat tour.
  • Pregnant or with back problems: speedboats bounce in chop; choose the longtail and check with your doctor.
  • More than 10 guests: see our private speedboat and catamaran charter pages for bigger boats.
  • Want limestone cliffs and lagoons: the Ang Thong private speedboat (from 16 December).

What to bring

  • Food and drinks if you prefer to picnic (a cool box is fine; avoid glass, and take all rubbish back).
  • Cash in small notes for the Koh Madsum island fee (about 50 THB per person), any Koh Rap fee and lunch on the islands.
  • Swimwear, towels, reef-safe sunscreen, hats and sunglasses.
  • Dry bags for phones and cameras.
  • Water shoes, and fins if you want them.

Good to know

  • Sea by month: January to September is best, with February to April calmest. October to December is the rainy season: light rain doesn't stop the trip, but strong wind can. The captain has the final say on routes and stops for safety. If we cancel for weather, you choose a full refund or a new date.
  • Booking ahead: two or three days is usually enough. From mid-December to mid-January and around Songkran (13–15 April), book a week or more ahead.
  • Seasickness: morning water is usually calmer, and the smoothest seats are towards the back.
  • Children: adult and child life jackets are on board, and children wear them at all times on the boat. Tell us children's ages when you book.
  • Mobility: boarding is from Thong Krut pier; at the islands you may step into shallow water.
  • The pigs: watch and photograph them, let them come to you, and don't chase, lift or feed them junk food.
  • Drones: registered drones only (CAAT and NBTC); keep clear of the animals and other visitors.

Pickup and meeting point

The boat leaves from Thong Krut pier on the south-west coast; we send the exact location and meeting time on WhatsApp. Hotel transfers can be arranged on request from the main areas of Koh Samui (Chaweng, Lamai, Bophut, Maenam, Choeng Mon, Bang Rak and Plai Laem). If the road to your villa is too narrow for a minibus, we send a nearby meeting point with a map pin. Thong Krut is about 45–60 minutes by road from Chaweng and 30–40 minutes from Lamai.
